title: Linkability of GPS coordinates across time and systems
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted in transit can be linked to identify the child's movements over time and potentially correlated with other data sources (e.g., device identifiers, timestamps) to create a detailed movement profile.

title: Identification of child from location data at backend
description: The Mobile App Backend can identify the child from the received GPS coordinates, especially when combined with other stored data (e.g., user profiles, device IDs, timestamps), creating a persistent location history.

title: Excessive data collection via continuous GPS tracking
description: The child's device transmits live GPS coordinates at regular intervals, which may be excessive for the stated purpose and violates data minimization principles by collecting more precise and frequent location data than necessary.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data at backend
description: The Mobile App Backend may store, process, or share the received GPS coordinates with third parties (e.g., advertisers, analytics services, or other systems) without proper authorization or consent.

title: Unnecessary Location Data Storage
description: The backend writes each location ping to the Location History Store. This represents an explicit data disclosure where personal location data is transferred to storage. The threat arises if the system stores more location data than strictly necessary for its intended purpose, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: Location data is personal data; the system may store more data than required for legitimate purposes.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as it represents explicit disclosure; tree_node selection based on general LINDDUN methodology.

title: Location Data Linkability
description: Location history data can be used to link different data points together, potentially revealing patterns of movement and associating them with other personal information. The data in transit (the flow itself) contains information that could be used to link the user's movements across time and space.
assumptions: Location data contains enough granularity to identify movement patterns; metadata or derived data could enable linking.
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 selected as it represents data-centric linkability threats in transit.

title: Location Data Identification
description: Location data can directly or indirectly identify individuals. The flow transmits personal location information that, when combined with timestamps and potentially other metadata, could be used to identify specific users or their whereabouts.
assumptions: Location data is personally identifiable; timestamps and patterns can be used for identification.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 selected as it represents identification threats in data in transit.

title: Insecure Location Data Storage
description: The Location History Store (DS1) receives and stores personal location data. If the store lacks proper access controls, encryption, or retention policies, this could lead to unauthorized access or excessive retention of sensitive location information.
assumptions: The destination element processes/stores data in ways that may expose it to unauthorized access or retention beyond necessity.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.2 represents implicit disclosure through storage practices; severity elevated due to sensitive nature of location data.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Location Data
description: Location data is sensitive personal data subject to regulations like GDPR. The destination element (DS1) must comply with data protection requirements including consent, purpose limitation, and data subject rights. Non-compliance could result in legal and reputational risks.
assumptions: Location data is classified as sensitive personal data under applicable regulations; the system must comply with data protection laws.
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 selected as it represents regulatory compliance threats at the destination; tree_node based on general LINDDUN methodology.

title: Location data used to link user to other data sources
description: Location pings transmitted in transit could contain metadata (timestamps, device identifiers) that enable linking this user's location data with other datasets, creating a comprehensive profile of movements and activities.
assumptions: Third parties or systems with access to the data flow can correlate location data with other identifiers
uncertainty_note: Assuming metadata is present in the data flow

title: Location data enables identification of individuals
description: Precise location pings transmitted between backend and geofencing engine could be used to identify specific individuals, especially when combined with timing information and known patterns of movement.
assumptions: Location data is precise enough to identify individuals or narrow down to small groups
uncertainty_note: Depends on precision of location data and context

title: Geofencing engine processes location data beyond stated purpose
description: The Geofencing Engine may process location data for purposes beyond simple zone entry/exit detection, potentially storing or sharing data with third parties without explicit consent or necessity.
assumptions: Geofencing engine has capabilities or incentives to use data beyond its primary function
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual implementation and data retention policies of P2

title: Excessive processing of location data at destination
description: The Geofencing Engine may process location data in ways that are not strictly necessary for geofencing functionality, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Processing goes beyond what is required for zone entry/exit detection
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual processing logic at P2

title: Location-based Linkability of Family Zone Definitions
description: Zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) transmitted from DS2 to P2 can be used to link the family account to specific physical locations and movement patterns, potentially revealing associations between family members and their routines.
assumptions: Zone definitions contain identifiable location information that can be correlated with other data sources
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for location-based linkability

title: Identifiability of Family Members Through Zone Processing
description: The Geofencing Engine (P2) processes zone definitions that may reveal sensitive information about family members' locations, routines, and associations, making them identifiable through their configured geofences.
assumptions: Zone definitions are processed in a way that preserves or reveals identifying information about family members
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for identifiability through data processing

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Zone Configuration Data
description: The Family Account Store (DS2) may share zone definition data with the Geofencing Engine without proper access controls, potentially exposing sensitive location information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or data sharing policies at the source element
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for disclosure at source

title: Location-based Linkability via Geofencing Notifications
description: The geofencing engine shares arrival/departure notifications that inherently contain location context, enabling linkage of an individual's movements across different zones and time periods. This creates a trail of location-based activities that can be correlated to identify patterns of behavior.

title: Location Data Disclosure During Transmission
description: Geofencing notifications transmitted over the data flow contain sensitive location metadata that could be intercepted or logged by unauthorized parties, revealing movement patterns and zone access information.

title: Location Data Disclosure at Destination
description: The parent system receives and processes location-based notifications that may be stored, indexed, or shared in ways that expose sensitive movement information beyond the intended scope of the geofencing functionality.

title: Child identification through parent registration
description: Parent provides child's name, DOB, and school information during account registration, enabling identification of the child through the parent's account.
assumptions: Child's personal data is stored and accessible through parent's account

title: Data interception during registration
description: Personal data transmitted during account registration could be intercepted and linked to identify the parent and child.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or protected

title: Unauthorized data access at backend
description: Mobile app backend may store or process the child's personal information in ways that could lead to unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: Backend may have insufficient access controls

title: Excessive personal data collection
description: Registration process collects extensive personal data (name, DOB, school, geofence zones) that may exceed what's necessary for account creation.
assumptions: Data minimization principles not fully applied

title: Identity theft during registration
description: Parent's identity information could be stolen during the account registration process.
assumptions: Identity verification may be insufficient

title: Parent denial of registration
description: Parent could deny registering the account or creating the child's profile, complicating accountability.
assumptions: No audit trail or verification mechanism

title: Backend non-compliance with data protection laws
description: Mobile app backend may not comply with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding child data.
assumptions: Backend may lack proper compliance measures

title: Excessive Personal Data Storage in Family Account Store
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2) receives and stores comprehensive personal data including account information, child profiles, and geofence zone data. This represents an explicit data disclosure where the system collects and retains more personal data than strictly necessary for the intended functionality, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: The system stores all received data without strict necessity assessment
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 from context as it addresses explicit disclosure; tree_node may need verification against full LINDDUN Pro methodology

title: Location data in transit could identify child's movements
description: Location data transmitted from parent to backend could be intercepted, revealing the child's current location or movement patterns, potentially identifying the child's whereabouts to unauthorized parties.

title: Location data could be linked to identify child
description: Location data in transit could be correlated with other data sources (e.g., device identifiers, timestamps) to link and identify the child's identity and movements.

title: Backend could disclose location data to unauthorized parties
description: The mobile app backend could improperly disclose the child's location data to unauthorized third parties, violating privacy expectations.

title: Backend may store excessive location data
description: The backend may retain location history longer or with more precision than necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles.

title: Location data could be intercepted and misused
description: Location data in transit could be intercepted by malicious actors and used for stalking, harassment, or other harmful purposes.

title: Location History Data Inherent Identifiability
description: Location history data inherently contains personally identifiable information about an individual's movements, patterns, and routines. Even without explicit identifiers, the data can be used to identify the user through their unique movement patterns and visited locations.
assumptions: Location history is associated with a specific user account and can be correlated with other data sources.

title: Location History Linkability with External Data
description: Location history data can be linked with other data sources (e.g., social media, purchase records, device identifiers) to create comprehensive user profiles and track individuals across different contexts and services.
assumptions: The backend may have access to or can correlate with other data sources that contain user information.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History at Backend
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) receives and processes location history data. If access controls are inadequate or the backend is compromised, unauthorized parties could access sensitive location information.
assumptions: The backend has proper access controls and security measures in place.

title: Location Data Transmission Compliance Risk
description: Location history is classified as sensitive personal data under GDPR and similar regulations. Transmitting this data without proper consent mechanisms, encryption, or compliance with data protection requirements may result in regulatory non-compliance.
assumptions: The system must comply with applicable data protection regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.).
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements may vary by jurisdiction.

title: Location metadata enables guardian linkage
description: Metadata about the source (parent EE1) and destination (secondary guardian) in the location data flow can be used to link the data to specific individuals, revealing which parent is sharing with which guardian and potentially inferring family relationships.
assumptions: Metadata accompanying the location data includes source/destination identifiers or timing patterns that can be correlated.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable fit for metadata-based linkability at flow level

title: Parent's sharing action reveals child's location
description: The parent's act of initiating location data sharing inherently reveals the child's current location to the secondary guardian, creating an identifiability risk for the child who may not have consented to this sharing.
assumptions: The child's location is being shared without the child's direct consent, and the parent's action of sharing is the mechanism that makes the location identifiable.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 applies to source-level identifiability through the act of sharing

title: Backend stores location data beyond intended scope
description: The mobile app backend (P1) may store the child's location data longer than necessary or share it with other system components, creating unauthorized disclosure risks beyond the intended secondary guardian.
assumptions: The backend processes and stores location data, and there's potential for retention or access beyond the immediate sharing purpose.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is a standard node for disclosure at destination; actual backend behavior would need verification

title: Location data linkability during transmission
description: Child's live location data transmitted in transit could be intercepted and linked with other data sources to reconstruct movement patterns and identify the child's routines and whereabouts.

title: Identifiability of child's whereabouts at guardian
description: Secondary guardian receives live location data that can be used to identify the child's real-time location, movements, and daily patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about the child's activities and habits.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of location data by guardian
description: Secondary guardian may share or disclose the child's location data to unauthorized third parties, violating the child's privacy expectations and potentially exposing the child to risks.

title: Usurpation of location data for unauthorized purposes
description: Secondary guardian may use the child's location data for purposes beyond the intended guardian role, such as stalking, harassment, or unauthorized surveillance.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics Data
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics shared in transit could potentially be linked with other data sources (e.g., device fingerprints, IP addresses, or partner data) to re-identify individual users or correlate their behavior patterns across services.

title: Unauthorized Use of Analytics Data
description: The advertising/analytics partner may use the shared aggregated analytics beyond the agreed purpose of funding the app's free tier, potentially for profiling, targeted advertising, or other purposes not consented to by users.

title: Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: The external partner may further share or sell the received analytics data to additional third parties, advertisers, or data brokers without user consent or beyond the original data sharing agreement.

title: Identification via Metadata in Transit
description: Metadata accompanying the analytics data in transit (e.g., timestamps, data volume patterns, or request/response patterns) could be used to infer information about the source system or individual user sessions.

title: Location data identifies child's whereabouts in transit
description: Location data transmitted in the check-in/SOS message can identify the child's precise location and movements while in transit, potentially revealing sensitive patterns of behavior or presence at specific locations.

title: Location data can be linked to other data sources
description: Location data in transit can be linked with other data (e.g., time stamps, device identifiers) to create a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and activities.

title: Location data interception during transmission
description: Location data transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, exposing the child's real-time location to potential threats.

title: Child's voluntary location sharing identifies them
description: The child's act of sharing location data voluntarily identifies their current whereabouts and can be used to track their movements.

title: Parent receives identifiable location data
description: The parent (destination) receives location data that directly identifies the child's precise location, enabling tracking and monitoring.
